Button

Khipu button

A button that steps through a few alternatives. From a run of one cord of an Inka khipu hang the ends of its real cords, one for each: the one you are on hangs plumb, and a press draws the next one plumb as it lays the last aside.

Wedding toast

Chat

Two minutes for my sister’s wedding toast. She’s a marine biologist; Tom, her husband, builds wooden boats.

Try opening on a rock pool: “When we were kids, Ana could sit by one rock pool for a whole afternoon. Tom is the first thing I’ve seen her look at that way.”

At the harbour

1 suggestion

We got down to the harbour just after six. The water was very calm, and Tom’s boat was the only one out.

Instead of “very calm”

flat calm

Reply to the Harbour Club

3 drafts
To bookings@harbourclub.example · Subject Saturday

Thank you, Saturday at six works for us. Could we have the long table by the window? We will be twenty-two.

The opening line
“Tom spent a winter building Ana a boat, and named it after a sea slug she discovered.”

# khipu-button A "next option" button for anything that steps through a few alternatives, such as the versions of a chat reply or an editor's suggestions. The end of one of an Inka khipu's two-colour cords runs across the button from under its left edge and ends in its own knot. From behind it hang the ends of the khipu's real cords, one for each option. The one you are on hangs plumb, and a press draws the next one plumb as it lays the last aside. The words beside them ("2 of 3 ›") are part of its name. This is the button part of `components/khipu` and nothing else. There is no conversation khipu, no tree and no essay. Every cord comes from one photograph: the Cleveland Museum of Art's khipu 1940.469 (CC0). Each cord on the button is one stretch of one real cord, cut in one piece on the photograph's own pixel grid (`assets/ends.webp`), with its own knotted or curled end. Nothing is drawn, straightened or joined. A cord only turns, as one rigid piece, about the point where it is tied on. ## Markup ```html ``` `[data-khipu-button]` starts by itself. Write the words in the HTML: without JS the button is a plain framed button that says "2 of 3 ›", with its words centred. The `›` says a press goes forward. It is `aria-hidden`, and the script adds it if you leave it out. Outside a form, a button with no `type` is given `type="button"`; inside one, give it `type="button"` yourself unless a press should also submit. ## Driving it The button does not own your content. It tells you which option to show: ```js const btn = document.querySelector('#versions'); btn.addEventListener('khipu-button:change', (e) => { const { current, count, from, dir, via } = e.detail; // 3, 3, 2, 'next', 'pointer' showVersion(current); }); ``` ```js import { khipuButton } from './khipu-button.js'; const kb = khipuButton(btn, { count: 3, current: 2, noun: 'version' }); // null above 7 options: see below kb.current; kb.count; // 2, 3 (1-based, like the words) kb.next(); kb.prev(); // step, as a press would kb.set(1, { say: true }); // jump; say: true also announces it in the live line kb.setCount(4, 4, { say: true }); // a fourth version arrived: its cord is tied on, and it is shown (false above 7) kb.ready; // a promise: the cords are on kb.state(); // for tests: each cord's resting angle, and which one is on kb.destroy(); // removes the cords, the live line and every listener; the button is its markup again ``` `setCount` with a new count keeps every cord where it was. The new cord fades in at the next tie along the primary, and the primary does not change. Give `data-max` for the most options there may be, and the room for their cords is kept from the start, so the button never widens and its neighbours never move. Without it, the button widens by one tie. After `destroy()` the controller does nothing, and a second `destroy()` is a no-op. `destroy()` writes the current option and count back to `data-current` and `data-count`, so `khipuButton(btn)` carries on where it was. **Seven options at most.** There is one cord for each option, and seven cords to cut, so keep a stepper's alternatives to seven. With more, `khipuButton()` leaves the button as it is (its own words, no cords, no steps) and returns `null`, and the auto-start does the same. `setCount()` above seven changes nothing and returns `false`, so you can stop offering more: hide or disable your Retry when it does. Both warn in the console. ## Options Data attributes, or the options object, which wins. | Option | Attribute | Default | | |---|---|---|---| | `count` | `data-count` | `2` | How many options, one cord each: **1 to 7**, because there are seven clean whole cord ends of one kind on the photograph. Above 7 the button is not taken over (see Driving it). | | `current` | `data-current` | `1` | The option shown, 1-based. | | `max` | `data-max` | the count | Keep room for this many cords, for options that may arrive later (`setCount`). | | `noun` | `data-noun` | `option` | For the name and the live line: "2 of 3, next version", then "Version 3 of 3". | | `label` | `data-label` | `{i} of {n}` | The visible words before the `›`. `{i}`, `{n}`, `{noun}` and `{Noun}` are filled in. | | `wrap` | `data-wrap` | `false` with a previous button, `true` without | `false`: it stops at the last option (and the previous button at the first). There it stays focusable but is `aria-disabled`, its name says "the last version", its `›` fades, and its cords keep their colour, so you can still see where you are. `true`: from the last option a press goes round to the first. That, and a jump by `set()` or `setCount()`, is the only time more than one cord changes side, and they go a cord at a time (see By hand). | | `prev` | `data-prev` | the `.kb-prev` in the same `.kb-pair` | The id of a "previous" button anywhere on the page. | | `status` | `data-status` | a line after the button | The id of your own live region. Use it when the button may be removed, so its last word is said from an element that stays. | | `src` | `data-src` | `assets/ends.json` beside the module | The cords' map. `ends.webp` sits beside it. | | | `data-label-fixed` | | Keep your own `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`). | ### Sizes Size is the class. The cords' box is most of the button's height. Its width follows from the number of options, and it never changes as you step. | class | button | the khipu it holds, top to bottom | where | |---|---|---|---| | `.kb` | 32 px | 3.8 cm | **the row size**: a reply's footer, a form footer, a list row | | `.kb-tool` | 44 px | 4.3 cm | a toolbar | | `.kb-lg` | 64 px | 4.8 cm | a choice on its own | | `.kb-xl` | 132 px (112 px on a screen 480 px wide or less) | 10 cm | **a hero**: the demo's opening line, with all seven cords (longer cords, not a larger picture) | | `.kb-sm` | 26 px | 3.4 cm | dense desktop lists only: on a phone it is a small target, and its cords are about 1.3 px wide | At every size up to `.kb-xl`, a 3x screen draws at most 0.82 of its pixels per pixel of the photograph, so the cords are never enlarged. Each size can show more of each cord (the larger, the longer), never a blown-up one. For any other size, set `--kb-h` (the button), `--kb-cords-h` (the cords' box), `--kb-fragment` (how much of the khipu the box holds, in the photograph's px, at about 44 to the centimetre) and `--kb-tie` (how far down that box the primary crosses, in the same px). A smaller fragment gives thicker cords. In a `.kb-pair` the previous button takes the height of the stepper beside it, at any size. The stepper has a hairline edge at rest, like the buttons around it. `.kb-quiet` swaps the hairline for a faint face, for a row of quiet text buttons. Either way the edge shows, because the primary runs on under it: the button is a window on a longer khipu. Theme with `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--ink-3`, `--rule` (the edge), `--accent` (the focus ring) and `--sans`. `--accent` must reach 3:1 against the surface behind the button. The demo's clay `#c96f4a` gives 3.15:1 on `--paper` and 3.3:1 on its cards, but only 2.85:1 on `--paper-2`, so pick a darker accent there. The cords are the photograph's colours, so they are not themed. They sit best on warm paper, close to the cloth they were photographed on. ## Events (all bubble) | | when | |---|---| | `khipu-button:change` | the option (or, after `setCount`, the count) changed. `detail: { current, count, from, dir, via }`: `dir` is `next` or `prev` for a step and `set` for `set()` or `setCount()`; `via` is `pointer`, `touch`, `key`, `api` or `other` (assistive tech, `el.click()`) | | `khipu-button:ready` | the cords are on (`detail: { current, count }`) | ## By hand - **Hover** (a real mouse only): the next cord lifts a little toward plumb, as if you had reached for it, and the edge darkens. The previous button does the same for the cord before. After a press the hint pauses for 0.7 s (after a sweep, until every cord is at rest), then comes back if the mouse is still there. - **Press and hold** (mouse, a held Space, or a touch): the face darkens and the next cord is drawn about half-way to plumb and held there. Let go and it is drawn plumb (0.62 s, a damped spring from rest), while the cord you were on is laid aside a beat later (0.8 s). Nothing spins, swings round or jumps. A cord turns about 24 degrees in a step. - **Touch** waits 100 ms before it takes hold, as the browser's own `:active` does, so a scroll that starts on the button never moves a cord. A tap steps on its click, as a native button does, so a tap that only stops a scrolling page stays inert, as theirs does. Until the click comes the cord stays as it is, so nothing starts back before it goes on. A touch held 0.45 s or more steps when it lifts on the button, because a long press may bring no click, and a click that still follows it is not counted again, however long your change handler takes. - **Slide off before letting go**, or start a scroll on it: the cord goes back, the face goes back, and nothing happens. - **Enter** steps at once. A held Enter steps once, not on and on. - **More than one option at once** (round from the last to the first with `wrap`, the default only without a previous button, or a jump by `set()` or `setCount()`): the cords go a cord at a time, from the one let go toward the one drawn, 180 ms apart (closer on a long jump, so that every start falls within 0.72 s). Each turns into the room its neighbour has just left, so no two cross, and each takes as long as its turn needs to stay under 115 degrees a second; a plain step's drawn cord peaks at about 150. Measured on the list's wrap from 4 to 1: the two cords that change side pass plumb 0.2 s apart, never more than one is near plumb at once, the peaks are 114 to 115 degrees a second, and all are at rest after 1.6 s. A cord tied on by `setCount()` fades in on its turn. ## Accessibility - It is a real `
